A desk voice companion running the Xiaozhi firmware

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad.

Unplug USB and disconnect any battery before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

31PRAT-WIRE-1

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire.
  2. These must not beep. Set the multimeter to continuity and probe each pair. A beep means a short: find it before you plug in.
    3V3GND5VGND3V3.2GND
  3. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    3V3Controller 3V3 · Microphone VDD
    GNDController G.2 · Microphone GND · Microphone L/R
    MIC_SCKController 5 · Microphone SCK
    MIC_WSController 4 · Microphone WS
    MIC_SDController 6 · Microphone SD
    5VController 5V · Amplifier VIN
    GNDController G · Amplifier GND
    SPK_DINController 7 · Amplifier DIN
    SPK_BCLKController 15 · Amplifier BCLK
    SPK_LRCController 16 · Amplifier LRC
    spk_+Speaker + · Amplifier SPK+
    spk_-Speaker - · Amplifier SPK-
    3V3.2Controller 3V3.2 · Display VCC
    GNDController G.3 · Display GND
    I2C_SDAController 41 · Display SDA
    I2C_SCLController 42 · Display SCL
    BTN_CHATController 0 · Chat 1
    BTN_TALKController 47 · Talk 1
    BTN_VOL_UPController 40 · Vol+ 1
    BTN_VOL_DOWNController 39 · Vol- 1
    GNDController G.4 · Chat 2 · Talk 2 · Vol+ 2 · Vol- 2
  4. Plug in. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug at once and go back to step 2.
  5. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
32PRAT-WIRE-1

Prat is built

Prat is a small box on your desk that you talk to: press and hold a button, speak, and an answer comes back from the speaker while a little OLED shows what it heard and how it feels. It is the Xiaozhi open-source project's breadboard build (ESP32-S3, INMP441 microphone, MAX98357A amplifier, SSD1306 display) made permanent: the same pin map, soldered, in a printed case. The ESP32 only handles audio, buttons and the screen; the conversation runs on a Xiaozhi server you configure.
